sourcedFrom: Safety & Instruction Manual Muzzleloading Rifle — ©2025 Thompson Center Arms, P/N 00084002 (2025)
cleanIntro: The Triumph is a break-action inline carrying T/C's Speed Breech XT plug — a quarter-turn plug with alignment marks that comes out in your fingers, not a threaded plug you wrench out. That one difference is why the Triumph has its own guide and why nothing here is shared with the Encore, Omega, Impact or Northwest Explorer. Everything below is quoted from the Triumph's own 2025 manual.

steps.title: Confirm the rifle is unprimed and uncharged
steps.action: Establish this first. A muzzleloader shows you nothing on its own, so the checks below are the whole verification.
steps.caution: Never attempt to clean a charged or primed muzzleloading firearm.
steps.quote: Ensure that the gun is unprimed and uncharged.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual Muzzleloading Rifle — ©2025 Thompson Center Arms, P/N 00084002 — Disassembly of the T/C® Triumph® — p.37

steps.title: Tip the trigger guard down and forward, then open the barrel
steps.action: The Triumph's action is released at the trigger guard and the barrel then tips open, exposing the primer pocket in the breech plug. Confirm there is no primer sitting in it.
steps.quote: Remove the breech plug from the Triumph® muzzleloader. To do this, tip the trigger guard down and forward and then tip the barrel open to be certain that there is no primer in the primer pocket.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual Muzzleloading Rifle — ©2025 Thompson Center Arms, P/N 00084002 — Thorough Cleaning — p.34

steps.title: Sight the ignition fire channel
steps.action: Hold the muzzle up to a light and look through the ignition fire channel from the breech. Light through it means the barrel is empty; no light means charged or obstructed, and either way you stop and unload.
steps.quote: Tip the barrel open and make sure that the gun is unprimed.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual Muzzleloading Rifle — ©2025 Thompson Center Arms, P/N 00084002 — Unloading a Charge from the Triumph® Muzzleloader — p.30
steps.warn: If you cannot see through the channel, the rifle is charged or obstructed. Do not proceed.

steps.title: If it is charged, pull the plug and let gravity unload it
steps.action: With the plug out and the muzzle up, powder falls clear of the breech. The projectile is then pushed out with the ramrod and its extension, or drawn with a bullet puller.
steps.quote: Once the breech plug has been removed, point the muzzle up. Gravity should then cause the pellets or the loose powder to drop out.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual Muzzleloading Rifle — ©2025 Thompson Center Arms, P/N 00084002 — Unloading and Uncharging Continued — p.31

steps.title: Turn the Speed Breech XT plug a quarter turn
steps.action: This is the Triumph's defining step and it is not a threaded plug. A quarter turn counter-clockwise, by hand or with the wrench, and the plug is unlocked — do not keep turning it as though it were threaded.
steps.caution: Use only Thompson/Center breech plugs of the correct type in the Triumph.
steps.quote: The breech plug is removed from the barrel by turning it 1/4 turn counter-clockwise (as viewed from the breech end of the barrel) by hand or using the wrench that was supplied with the gun.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual Muzzleloading Rifle — ©2025 Thompson Center Arms, P/N 00084002 — Thorough Cleaning — p.34

steps.title: Align the marks and withdraw the plug by hand
steps.action: The barrel and plug carry reference marks. When they line up the plug is free and lifts straight out. If drag holds it, a tap from the ramrod down the bore frees it.
steps.aside: The manual notes you may need the wrench simply to overcome initial barrel-to-plug drag.
steps.quote: When the reference marks on the barrel and breech plug are aligned, the breech plug can be withdrawn from the barrel with just your fingers.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual Muzzleloading Rifle — ©2025 Thompson Center Arms, P/N 00084002 — Thorough Cleaning — p.35

steps.title: Remove the ramrod
steps.action: Slide the ramrod out of the thimbles and set it aside before any further takedown.
steps.quote: Remove the ramrod from the thimbles - set it aside.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual Muzzleloading Rifle — ©2025 Thompson Center Arms, P/N 00084002 — Takedown of the Triumph® Muzzleloader — p.38

steps.title: Run the bore, then clean the trigger guard assembly
steps.action: Jag onto the ramrod, patch soaked in black-powder solvent, up and down the bore until the fouling is gone, then dry patches until the bore is dry. Then take a soft bristle brush to the trigger guard assembly, dry it and lightly oil it.
steps.prose: Black-powder residue is corrosive. Fouling also raises pressure shot to shot, so a dirty bore is an accuracy problem before it is a rust problem.
steps.aside: The manual's bore instruction on the same page: after removing all the fouling, follow up with a few dry patches to thoroughly dry the bore.
steps.quote: Clean the trigger guard assembly with a soft bristle brush dampened with some bore cleaner. When the trigger guard is dry, lightly oil it.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual Muzzleloading Rifle — ©2025 Thompson Center Arms, P/N 00084002 — Field Cleaning — p.33

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Barrel clear, Speed Breech plug out, bore and trigger guard serviced. That is routine maintenance on the Triumph. Taking the barrel off the receiver and servicing the plug's O-ring is the manual's own disassembly section, and it is in the Deep Clean.
steps.quote: If the Triumph® muzzleloading rifle has become very dirty due to extensive firing, the shooter may want to disassemble the rifle further than just removing the breech plug.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual Muzzleloading Rifle — ©2025 Thompson Center Arms, P/N 00084002 — Thorough Cleaning — p.36

deepSteps.title: Scrub the plug and anti-seize it
deepSteps.action: Get the fouling off the plug and clean the barrel's breech end with a stiff brush and solvent. Dry both, then anti-seize before the plug goes back.
deepSteps.quote: Once removed, the breech plug should be scrubbed free of fouling and should then be lubricated with an anti-seize lubricant like T/C’s Super Lube, before reinstallation.
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual Muzzleloading Rifle — ©2025 Thompson Center Arms, P/N 00084002 — Thorough Cleaning — p.35

deepSteps.title: Take the forend off
deepSteps.action: Two screws hold the forend to its hangers on the barrel. Back them out and lift the forend clear — this has to happen before the barrel can leave the receiver.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the forend from the barrel by removing the two forend screws.
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual Muzzleloading Rifle — ©2025 Thompson Center Arms, P/N 00084002 — Takedown of the Triumph® Muzzleloader — p.38

deepSteps.title: Free the trigger guard pivot pin
deepSteps.action: Back off the pivot pin retaining screw with a 1/16 inch hex wrench — only far enough to release the pin, the manual is explicit that it need not come all the way out — then push the trigger guard pivot pin out in either direction.
deepSteps.aside: The manual notes you do not have to completely remove the set screw — loosen it only enough to allow the pin to be pushed out.
deepSteps.quote: Push the trigger guard pivot pin out - in either direction.
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual Muzzleloading Rifle — ©2025 Thompson Center Arms, P/N 00084002 — Takedown of the Triumph® Muzzleloader — p.38

deepSteps.title: Remove the barrel hinge pin retaining screw
deepSteps.action: This one wants correctly fitted flat screwdrivers on both ends of the assembly at once. A single blade on one end will cam out and chew the slot.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the barrel hinge pin retaining screw (using correctly fitted flat screwdrivers on each end of this assembly).
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual Muzzleloading Rifle — ©2025 Thompson Center Arms, P/N 00084002 — Takedown of the Triumph® Muzzleloader — p.38

deepSteps.title: Push the barrel pivot pin out and separate the barrel
deepSteps.action: With the retaining screw gone the pivot pin drives out and the barrel comes off the receiver. That is the Triumph in its two groups — stock-and-receiver, and barrel assembly.
deepSteps.quote: Push the barrel pivot pin out of the receiver - allowing the barrel to become detached from the receiver at this point.
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual Muzzleloading Rifle — ©2025 Thompson Center Arms, P/N 00084002 — Takedown of the Triumph® Muzzleloader — p.38
deepSteps.warn: Never disassemble the rifle beyond the procedures outlined in the manual.

deepSteps.title: Install the plug the right way up and lock it 90 degrees
deepSteps.action: The Speed Breech plug is stamped UP and it goes in that way. It locks with a 90 degree clockwise turn — by hand or with the wrench — not by threading it down tight.
deepSteps.caution: Install the breech plug with the “UP” marking on top.
deepSteps.quote: The breech plug must be locked into place by turning it clockwise 90 degrees by hand - or with the breech plug wrench provided.
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual Muzzleloading Rifle — ©2025 Thompson Center Arms, P/N 00084002 — Thorough Cleaning — p.36

cleaning.name: Bore
tasks: Solvent-soaked patches on the supplied jag until they come out clean
Dry patches until the bore is dry
Light lubricant on the bore once it is completely dry

cleaning.name: Speed Breech XT plug
tasks: Scrub the plug free of fouling
Inspect the replaceable heat-resistant O-ring; replace with T/C #7531 if damaged
Leave the gas rings alone — they are a permanent assembly with the plug and are cleaned in place
Anti-seize the plug and the barrel's breech area before reinstalling
Check the UP marking is on top when it goes back

cleaning.name: Receiver and trigger group
tasks: Soft bristle brush with bore cleaner over the trigger guard assembly, then dry and lightly oil
Moisture-displacing oil into the firing pin within the frame, from front and back
Wipe powder residue from the hammer/trigger assembly and receiver and dry it
Remove fouling from the receiver and exterior with an oily cotton cloth

reassembly: Fit the barrel to the receiver and drive the barrel pivot pin home
Refit the barrel hinge pin retaining screw with correctly fitted flat screwdrivers
Push the trigger guard pivot pin back in and retighten its retaining screw
Refit the forend with its two screws
Anti-seize the plug, seat it with the UP marking on top and lock it 90 degrees clockwise
Return the ramrod to the thimbles
fncheck: With the rifle unprimed and uncharged, check the barrel latch and the hammer/trigger mechanism for proper function before loading and firing — the manual requires this after the breech plug has been reinstalled.
